clue.text: Dickensian with a standing proposal

parts.note: a Dickens character in David Copperfield whose marriage offer, 'is willin'', is sent again and again until accepted

explanation.surface: A Victorian character keeps a marriage offer permanently on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: In David Copperfield the carrier sends Peggotty the message that he 'is willin'' and repeats it until she marries him, so the proposal stands.
explanation.definitionFit: The carrier in David Copperfield is the Dickens figure famous for a repeated offer of marriage.

clue.text: A programme to watch for a spell?

definitions.text: A programme to watch for a spell?

parts.words: A programme to watch for a spell?
parts.note: a spell here is a magic charm, not a period of time, and the programme is what a charmed person must go through

explanation.walkthrough: 'watch for a spell' suggests viewing something for a while; the spell is an enchantment.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed under a magic charm, as by a witch.

clue.text: University has the first of three rudiments of learning

definitions.meaning: the University of ..., in Berkshire, England

definitions.text: the first of three rudiments of learning
definitions.meaning: the three Rs, the basics of schooling, are ..., writing and arithmetic

explanation.walkthrough: The 'three Rs' are a British phrase for basic schooling: reading, (w)riting and (a)rithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A town with a well-known English university, and the skill of making sense of text, first of the basic skills.

clue.text: One of Joseph's purchasers

parts.note: in Genesis 37 Joseph's brothers sell him to a caravan of traders descended from Abraham's son by Hagar

explanation.walkthrough: Genesis says Joseph was sold for twenty pieces of silver to traders bound for Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the desert tribe said to descend from Abraham's son by Hagar, who bought Joseph.

clue.text: Taking a call in an unusual pose — quite a dish !

indicators.note: the call is set inside the rearranged letters of the pose
an unusual pose is one put into an odd new arrangement, so its letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone answers the phone while striking an awkward posture, and looks rather attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns POSE into ESOP, and 'in' puts CALL inside it: ES-CALL-OP. 'Taking a call' reads as answering the phone; 'dish' is both food and an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallop, also spelt with an E in front, is a shellfish served as a dish.

clue.text: Gladiator of Lacedaemonian origin ?

parts.note: Lacedaemon is Sparta, and the famous rebel gladiator's name seems to begin with that city

explanation.walkthrough: The rebel gladiator was in fact a Thracian; the question mark admits his name only looks Spartan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thracian gladiator who led the slave revolt against Rome in 73 BC.

clue.text: The second son of a Babylonian idol

parts.note: Bel, the Babylonian god of the apocryphal story Bel and the Dragon

explanation.surface: A Babylonian statue apparently has two sons.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis makes him the younger son of Adam and Eve, killed by his brother Cain.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis he is the younger child of Adam and Eve, born after Cain.

clue.text: Has she her fair share of pride ?

definitions.text: Has she her fair share of pride ?

parts.words: Has she her fair share of pride ?
parts.note: a pride is a group of big cats, and she is a female member of one

explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' looks like vanity, but a group of lions is called a pride.
explanation.definitionFit: A female big cat of the kind that lives in a pride.

clue.text: One type of devotion

parts.note: religious reverence is one kind of dedication

explanation.definitionFit: Religious reverence and dutiful observance are a form of devoutness.

clue.text: Worrying kind of work ?

definitions.meaning: being anxious, as a noun or verb sense of fretting
decorative cut-out woodwork is named fretwork

explanation.walkthrough: The definitions sit side by side; 'work' is fretwork, made with a fine saw.
explanation.definitionFit: To be anxious, and the ornamental pattern that gives fretwork its name.

clue.text: Rain or shine it's under clerical control

definitions.meaning: examples of conditions outside on a given day
the 'clerk of the ...' is the old jocular figure imagined to arrange rain and sun

explanation.walkthrough: 'clerical' suggests the clergy, but it refers to the imaginary clerk who manages the skies.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain and sunshine are both kinds of atmospheric conditions, which an old joke puts in the charge of a clerk.

clue.text: Flower of wind and sea

parts.note: one name covers a garden bloom nicknamed the windflower and a tentacled creature of rock pools

explanation.walkthrough: The plant's name comes from the Greek for wind, hence 'windflower', and the same name, with 'sea' in front, is a marine animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant is called the windflower, and its namesake sea creature looks like a flower on the seabed.

clue.text: Like Gaul, according to Caesar

parts.note: Caesar's Gallic War opens by saying all Gaul is divided into three parts

explanation.walkthrough: The Latin schoolbook line is 'Gallia est omnis divisa in partes tres'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something split into three sections, as Caesar described Gaul.

clue.text: Half a sheet of paper ?

parts.note: the name of a standard paper size sounds like the French prefix meaning half

explanation.walkthrough: The paper size is a full sheet, not half of one; the question mark flags that its name echoes 'demi', half.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional British size of printing and writing paper whose name recalls the French for half.

clue.text: Pointing out we've got one of our moods

definitions.meaning: in English grammar the mood of plain statements, beside imperative and subjunctive

explanation.walkthrough: 'moods' looks emotional; it is grammar, the verb form for statements.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing or signalling, and the grammatical mood used for statements of fact.

clue.text: For a bargain-hunter it's healthier to sit astride a horse

indicators.note: one word sits on either side of the other, as a rider straddles a mount

parts.note: hale means healthy, so healthier is haler
gee-gee is a child's word for a horse, GG

explanation.surface: Advice that riding is good for your health, aimed at a shopper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sit astride' puts HA-LER either side of GG, the nursery word gee-gee.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who argues over price is trying to get a good deal.

clue.text: A regular visitor from outer space

definitions.text: A regular visitor from outer space

parts.words: A regular visitor from outer space
parts.note: cosmic rays and solar energy reach the earth constantly from beyond the atmosphere

explanation.walkthrough: The visitor sounds like a Martian; it is the cosmic and solar energy that keeps arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: Energy streaming to earth as rays from the sun and space.

clue.text: Vote of thanks from a Galilean village for the game ?

parts.note: Cana, the village of the wedding feast in John's Gospel; 'from' it makes the possessive Cana's
ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: A village in Galilee thanks someone for providing a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'vote of thanks from Cana' as CANA'S TA. Cana in Galilee is where water was turned into wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A rummy-style card game played with two packs.

clue.text: The state of " as you was before you were '

definitions.text: The state of " as you was before you were

parts.words: The state of " as you was before you were
parts.note: the time before someone was born, put in comic ungrammatical speech

explanation.walkthrough: 'As you was' is also a parade-ground command; here it means 'as you were' before birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurring or existing before birth, during pregnancy.

clue.text: In receipt of a card from Uncle Sam

definitions.text: In receipt of a card from Uncle Sam

parts.words: In receipt of a card from Uncle Sam
parts.note: Uncle Sam is the US government, and the card it sends young men is a call-up notice

explanation.walkthrough: The card sounds like a greeting, but it is the notice of conscription into the US forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscripted into military service in the United States.

clue.text: Not the present condition

parts.note: being away rather than here, the opposite of being in attendance

explanation.walkthrough: 'present' suggests the current time, but it means being here.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being away, the opposite of being here.

clue.text: Indulge in winter sport with William returning for the pot

parts.note: to ski is to take part in a winter sport

indicators.note: the name is read coming back, from its end to its start

parts.note: William Tell, the Swiss archer

explanation.surface: A skiing holiday with a friend called William ends in a trip back home for a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns TELL into LLET after SKI. William here is the legendary archer, not Bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A frying pan or small long-handled cooking vessel.

clue.text: On board they cause not the fall of man but his elevation

definitions.text: On board they cause not the fall of man but his elevation

parts.words: On board they cause not the fall of man but his elevation
parts.note: in the board game snakes and ... the snakes send a player's piece down and the other pieces send it up

explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship and 'the fall of man' the serpent in Eden; on the games board the snake brings a piece down while these raise it.
explanation.definitionFit: The climbing devices in snakes and ladders that carry a counter upward.

clue.text: The end of golden lads and girls, and chimney-sweepers

definitions.text: The end of golden lads and girls, and chimney-sweepers

parts.words: The end of golden lads and girls, and chimney-sweepers
parts.note: from the song in Cymbeline, 'Golden lads and girls all must, As chimney-sweepers, come to' this

explanation.walkthrough: The Shakespeare dirge 'Fear no more the heat o' the sun' says all, rich and poor, end as powder; chimney-sweepers are also coated in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine powdery remains, what every mortal becomes after death.

clue.text: Hands up in the peerage !

definitions.meaning: 'put up your ...' is slang for raising the fists to fight
the highest rank of British nobleman

explanation.walkthrough: Fists are 'dukes' in old boxing slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for fists raised to fight, and the noblemen of top rank.

clue.text: Inn had mead, served perhaps by her ?

definitions.text: Inn had mead, served perhaps by her ?

indicators.note: the letters are dished out in a fresh order, as drink is served round

explanation.surface: An old inn offered honey wine, maybe poured by a serving girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served perhaps' rearranges INN HAD MEAD, and the whole clue pictures the serving maid herself.
explanation.definitionFit: A female servant, the sort who might pour drinks at an inn.

clue.text: One of the palmy days?

parts.note: palmy means prosperous, but here it hints at a palm tree's fruit, which shares its name with a day of the calendar

explanation.walkthrough: 'palmy days' are good times; the fruit of one palm has the same name as a calendar day.
explanation.definitionFit: A day of the calendar, and the fruit of a palm tree.

clue.text: The trio can put on quite an act !

indicators.note: the trio stages a performance, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Three performers can stage a really entertaining show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can put on' rearranges TRIO. An uproarious performance is a riot, and the Riot Act is a famous act too.
explanation.definitionFit: A hugely funny performance or show, as in 'the show was a hoot'.

clue.text: The Sun King of a modern Thor

definitions.text: The Sun King of a modern Thor

parts.words: The Sun King of a modern Thor
parts.note: Thor Heyerdahl named his 1947 balsa raft after an Inca sun god

explanation.walkthrough: The Sun King suggests Louis XIV, and Thor the Norse god; the modern Thor is the Norwegian explorer who sailed the Pacific by raft.
explanation.definitionFit: The raft of the Norwegian explorer was named for the Inca solar deity.

clue.text: Wherewith one rules the waves ?

parts.note: Britannia, who rules the waves in the song, holds a three-pronged spear, as does Neptune

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rule, Britannia!' says Britannia rules the waves; she is pictured holding the sea god's three-pronged spear.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-pronged spear carried by Neptune and Britannia as a sign of mastery of the sea.

clue.text: My mistress, a pretty tripper

parts.note: from the song 'O mistress mine' in Twelfth Night: 'Trip no further, pretty' darling

explanation.walkthrough: The Shakespeare song addresses the mistress and tells her to trip no further; 'tripper' sounds like a day tourist.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a sweetheart, used of the beloved in Twelfth Night.

clue.text: A beast of a Western art supporter

parts.note: an easel holds a painting up while the artist works

explanation.surface: A horrible person turns out to be an American patron of the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beast' and 'art supporter' suggest a person; the supporter is a painter's stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A small slender carnivorous mammal.
